Hi all —

Quick baseline and clarifications from pricing:

- Baseline hosted API: $0.0009 per input token, $0.0012 per output token (example tier; final will be in the rate card).
- Discounting: we offer volume bands (monthly committed tokens) and multi-month commitment discounts. For this pilot scope we can discuss a 15% committed-benchmark discount starting at 5M tokens/month.

On the token attribution rules (short version):
- Input tokens = system tokens + user tokens + any tool-call arguments that are sent to the model.
- Output tokens = tokens emitted by the model as the response text.
- Tool-executed content (the payload returned by a third-party tool run) is billed as output tokens if that content is returned in the model response payload. If you invoke a tool and the tool's content is returned as a separate payload (not synthesized by the model), we treat the tool-returned bytes as output tokens for the purposes of metering because they are delivered back to the customer as "response content."

Rounding: we bill at the request level and round up fractional token counts to the nearest whole token at the final per-request tally. With streaming, tokens are accumulated server-side and the final settled token count for that request is used for billing; interim chunks are not billed separately. In practice that means a 0.7 fractional token from an incremental chunk is not billed until the request completes and the aggregate rounds up.

I'll attach an initial rate card draft (redwood_ratecard_q1_v1.pdf) and can produce a couple worked examples in CSV form. Laura — can you confirm if your team needs invoice-level rounding rules (summary vs per-request)? Some finance teams want global invoice-level rounding for easier reconciliation.

If helpful, I can also provide an example table: request A: system(50) + user(30) => input 80 tokens; model output 140 => output 140; total billed tokens = input 80 (at input rate) + output 140 (at output rate). For the tool example: request B: system(50)+user(40)+tool-arg(10)=input 100; model emits a tool-call and then we return tool payload (120) as part of the response => output 120 (billed as output).

Next steps: I'll put together the worked_examples-sheet.csv with a few rows.

A couple of finance items from our side:

- We need the exact per-request rounding rule documented in the SOW: "per-request rounding up to nearest token at final aggregation" is fine, but Finance also wants an example showing aggregated invoice math (e.g., if per-request rounding creates +0.3 tokens average per request at N requests, how that maps to the invoice total and whether we ever apply invoice-level truncation).
